name: Asset register and equipment records
one_line: The controlled population of owned production, inspection and utility equipment held as one standing document: the file's ROWS ARE ASSETS, each carrying a stable identity, an installed position and a standing lifecycle obligation, rather than records ABOUT one asset. The schema default's site-then-asset-then-record-type branch cannot place it, because a register has no single asset value to branch on. It is not one purchase, not one performed job, not a calibration outcome, not a depreciation schedule, and not an IT estate merely because equipment carries a serial number. Placeholder template on the fieldless manufacturing schema; it declares no field rows under PR-6 and serialises no destination dimensions.

proposed_fields.why_no_existing_key: SECONDING, NOT MINTING. The manufacturing schema anchor already proposes `asset` for the enduring machine that receives maintenance, calibration and inspection records, and engineering.commissioning-handover deliberately adopted the same spelling rather than minting a variant. This row seconds it and supplies the population-level evidence that makes it necessary. No canonical key covers it: `repository` is software, `camera_information` describes capture equipment, `project` is bounded work, and `location` is the Photos capture-place role rather than an installed operating position.
proposed_fields.destination_eligible_why: Seconded TRUE, but with a restriction this row is the reason for: `asset` is a destination dimension only for a file that HAS one asset value — a single-asset card or history index. A multi-asset register export has no single value and must not be forced under an asset level; it belongs at the site level as the site's population document.
proposed_fields.validation_rule_family: asset-tag pattern occurring in a labelled Asset, Equipment, Instrument or Machine slot, corroborated by register-row structure or a local controlled asset list. A serial number or an identifier-shaped token alone never validates it. R2/R6 own the pattern; this row writes no regex and no threshold.
proposed_fields.adjudication_note: Adjudicate once, on the manufacturing schema, in R1c. This row must not be counted as a competing private proposal. See NJ-MFG-ASSET-3 and manufacturing.calibration-record's NJ-CAL-1 on whether one `asset` key can carry both the producing machine and the measuring instrument.

proposed_fields.why_no_existing_key: SECONDING, NOT MINTING. The manufacturing schema anchor already proposes `site` for the facility that controls an asset. Canonical `location` is the Photos capture-location role and may differ from the installed operating location; `organization` names a custodian rather than a plant or a line; `institution` is a financial issuer.
proposed_fields.destination_eligible_why: Seconded TRUE, and it is the ONLY level this row can offer for a multi-asset register. For a genuinely single-site corpus the template validator should flatten the one-child level.
proposed_fields.reliability_why: A labelled Plant, Site, Facility, Area, Line or Functional Location slot can support it directly. An address, a company name or a filename token stays possible, because it may name a supplier, an issuing laboratory or a document custodian rather than the plant the equipment stands in.
proposed_fields.adjudication_note: Adjudicate once, on the manufacturing schema, in R1c; see the anchor's NJ-MFG-3 on site-versus-capture-location.

template.why: Empty by placeholder contract: `asset` and `site` remain proposals on the fieldless manufacturing schema. The researched recommendation, held as prose for R1c: site or line, then asset — with the asset level used ONLY for a file that carries one asset value, such as an asset card or a history index. A multi-asset register export has no single asset value and must sit at the site level as that site's population document; forcing it under an asset level would require inventing an asset fact the file does not carry. Record type is deliberately absent: the register itself is the constant situation, so a record-type level would be a single-child level for every branch. No asset-class level is proposed, because no such key is licensed anywhere on the roster and inventing one here would be padding. Not time-first: "For document and record domains, project, function, or subject usually comes before time because putting year first scatters related work across calendar folders." Annual exports and reviewed snapshots are versions of one enduring register; a year-first order would split that version family. The user may reverse, remove or flatten any of this after facts are validated.

collides_with.signal: SAME FIXTURE BOTH SIDES: `CNC network and maintenance inventory.csv` carries Machine No, Asset Tag, Line, Criticality, Next PM, Hostname, IP Address and OS Version on the same rows. P6 activation step 3 and P8 must count machine-number, line, criticality and next-PM evidence toward this row, and hostname, operating-system, licence-entitlement and network-address evidence toward business_operations.it-asset-inventory; the shared asset tag counts toward neither side by itself. This row owns the controlled production-equipment population and its lifecycle obligations; that row owns device configuration, entitlement and the network estate. The neighbour states the identical discriminator from its side.

SAME FIXTURE BOTH SIDES: the same maintenance system exports either `Asset card CNC-07.pdf` or `Work order history CNC-07 2019-2026.xlsx`, and both carry the equipment identifier, dates and an interval. This row owns the file when its ROWS ARE ASSETS and its columns state what is permanently true of each machine — manufacturer, serial, in-service date, position, cost centre, criticality, next-due interval. That row owns the file when its ROWS ARE EVENTS against a machine — job identifier, date, planned-or-corrective type, failure code, downtime, labour. Discriminated by what a row IS, not by the presence of an asset column: a register with a Next PM Due column is still this row's, and a history with an equipment column is still theirs. Wording aligned with the neighbour's own signal.

SAME FIXTURE BOTH SIDES: `Calibration due list 2026-Q4.xlsx`. This row owns it when its rows are durable population attributes only — instrument identifier, description, area, custodian, class, nominal interval, next due — with no per-instrument result. That row owns it when its rows carry a calibration outcome or an as-found status, which makes the file dated evidence that calibrations happened. Discriminated by the presence of a calibration-outcome column; an instrument roster stays here even when every row carries a next-due date, because a due date is a scheduling attribute of the population. Wording aligned with the neighbour's own signal.

SAME FIXTURE BOTH SIDES: `Fleet list - inspection due 2026.xlsx` — one row per asset with identifiers, in-service dates and intervals on both sides. This row owns rows that are fixed or site-bound equipment carried for capital, criticality and maintenance-planning reasons, with a location or cost-centre column and no road-use obligation; that row owns rows carrying registration-shaped identifiers, plated weights and statutory test dates, because those columns exist only because of an external roadworthiness duty. A forklift row sits here, a van row sits there, and a table holding both is a genuine mixed file that should group without either row copying its facts onto the other's rows. Wording aligned with the neighbour's own signal.

SAME FIXTURE BOTH SIDES: `Equipment and Spares Master.xlsx` holds equipment rows and replaceable-part rows under one set of Item, Description, Location, Status and Quantity columns. P6/P8 must count stable equipment identity plus installed functional location plus a standing lifecycle obligation toward this row, and stock code plus quantity, bin, reorder level and compatible-equipment evidence toward manufacturing.spare-parts. An item number and a location discriminate neither. The deciding question is whether a row names a thing that is INSTALLED and maintained or a thing that is HELD and consumed.

SAME FIXTURE BOTH SIDES: `Asset Handover Schedule - Line 3.xlsx`, the same physical units on opposite sides of a transfer, keyed on the same proposed `asset` handle. That row owns the units as DELIVERABLES — as-built definition, acceptance evidence, outstanding punch items, warranty start, the dossier that travels with them. This row owns the same units as OPERATED assets — register rows, criticality, maintenance regime, in-service history. The handover schedule is literally the seed of the register; a takeover signature block and punch-item references support that row, while in-service status updates and a maintenance regime support this one. Recorded here as a collision because CONNECTION.md section 5 types `role_split` as field-to-field only; see NJ-MFG-ASSET-2.

falls_through_to.why: A standalone manual, warranty card, equipment certificate or isolated asset card with durable purpose but insufficient population or controlled-asset context is exactly 00's "standalone certificates, notices, confirmations, forms, and PDFs that have a durable purpose but no broader group."

A purchase invoice, delivery note, packing list or disposal acknowledgement proving only a transaction and not standing asset control belongs with 00's "isolated invoices, delivery confirmations, booking records, boarding passes, purchase receipts, event tickets, and similar transactional documents."

An isolated equipment photograph with no readable tag, no register structure and no accepted asset group is one of 00's "images with no event, project, reference collection, or photo-family association" and must not acquire an asset fact.

An OCR-poor equipment list, a mixed plant-and-vehicle table, or a workbook whose finance, IT and plant column roles are unresolved is a file "whose meaning is partly understood but whose final location requires a future decision."

sensitivity_why: The harm here is AGGREGATION, and it differs in kind from the schema default's single-record exposure: one register file discloses the complete productive capability of a plant — every machine, its exact installed position, its criticality ranking, its condition and its service vulnerabilities — in a way no single work order does. Retirement and disposal registers additionally disclose forward plans. Custodian and responsible-worker names appear in register columns; they remain search and privacy observations and never become destination dimensions. The operational consequence this row asks of review: a compact evidence packet should carry column ROLES and row counts rather than register contents, because excerpting a register means excerpting the plant. The row assigns no handling class, and privacy policy must run before any model or connector sees register rows.
open_question: NEEDS-JOSEPH NJ-MFG-ASSET-1: when one workbook holds a maintenance/custody sheet and a depreciation sheet for the same machines, should review present a single multi-schema file with sheet-level evidence spans, or require the user to choose a primary placement after both schemas activate? The catalogue can state the boundary but cannot decide the review interaction. NJ-MFG-ASSET-2: engineering.commissioning-handover authored a `role_split` entry naming this DOMAIN, but CONNECTION.md section 5 types `role_split` as field-to-field, living in the canonical field list. R1c should decide whether that entry is re-typed as a `collides_with` (as this row has recorded it) or whether the edge vocabulary gains a domain-to-domain lifecycle-handover relation; this row must not edit a neighbour to resolve it. NJ-MFG-ASSET-3: the proposed `asset` key is asked to carry a producing machine here, a measuring instrument in manufacturing.calibration-record (its NJ-CAL-1) and a delivered installed instance in engineering.commissioning-handover; decide whether one key with a role distinction suffices or whether a canonical role split is required. NJ-MFG-ASSET-4: a multi-asset register carries no single `asset` value, so `asset` is destination-eligible for some files on this row and not others; decide whether destination eligibility can legitimately be per-file rather than per-field, or whether the register must instead be modelled as a site-level document that simply never uses the asset level. Until R1c answers, this placeholder correctly declares fields: [] and dimension_order: [].
